headline.title: The Meta hack shows there’s more to AI security than Mythos
headline.summary: Attackers exploited Meta's AI customer support agent to steal Instagram accounts by requesting the linking of accounts to their own email addresses. This incident highlights vulnerabilities in AI security, as one attacker even accessed a dormant Obama White House account to post pro-Iran content.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic May Be Rivals, but Investors Aren’t Picking Sides
articles.summary: Investors are showing interest in both OpenAI and Anthropic, viewing them as complementary players in the AI space rather than direct competitors. This perspective allows for diversified investment in leading AI technologies, similar to investing in both Pepsi and Coke.

articles.title: Mira Murati steps back into the spotlight, carefully
articles.summary: Mira Murati, a prominent figure in the AI industry, is re-emerging into the public eye to reinforce her presence in a competitive market. This shift comes as industry leaders recognize the need to actively engage and maintain visibility amid evolving dynamics.

articles.title: Why Apple Might Put Cameras Into Its Next AirPods
articles.summary: Apple is exploring the integration of cameras into its next generation of AirPods, but faces challenges related to battery life and privacy concerns. The potential feature aims to enhance functionality, though its implementation remains uncertain.

articles.title: AI Has Come for Serif Fonts
articles.summary: AI companies are increasingly adopting serif fonts in their designs to convey a sense of humanity and warmth. However, critics have labeled this trend as "tasteslop," suggesting a lack of originality and quality in the aesthetic choices.

articles.title: Seoul Purpose: How NVIDIA and South Korea Are Building the Future of AI
articles.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is visiting Seoul to engage with South Korean partners and innovators in AI and robotics, highlighting the country's role as a global hub for AI development. The collaboration aims to enhance sovereign AI infrastructure and support the vibrant gaming community in South Korea.

articles.title: Defense tech, AI, and fundraising take center stage at StrictlyVC Los Angeles on June 18
articles.summary: On June 18, The Aerospace Corporation Campus will host the StrictlyVC event, bringing together investors, founders, and tech leaders to discuss key developments in venture capital, defense technology, artificial intelligence, and advanced industries. Attendees can secure their spots for an evening of insightful conversations on these critical topics.

articles.title: Beyond Output Matching: Preserving Internal Geometry in NVFP4 LLM Distillatio
articles.summary: The article discusses a new approach to quantization-aware distillation (QAD) for low-precision inference in large language models, specifically focusing on NVFP4-based methods. It emphasizes the importance of preserving internal geometry during the distillation process to improve accuracy while reducing computational costs.

articles.title: Edit-R2: Context-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Image Editing
articles.summary: The paper introduces Edit-R2, a context-aware reinforcement learning framework designed for multi-turn image editing, allowing users to iteratively refine images through a series of instructions. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods that primarily focus on single-turn editing by incorporating session-level constraints to maintain coherence across multiple editing steps.

articles.title: Boosting Brain-to-Image Decoding with TRIBE v2 Data Augmentation
articles.summary: Researchers have explored the use of TRIBE v2, a pretrained model of fMRI responses, to enhance brain-to-image decoding by augmenting small datasets with synthetic data. Their findings suggest that this approach can effectively improve decoding performance in low-data scenarios.

articles.title: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
articles.summary: The article introduces CUA-HandCrafted, a public benchmark consisting of 793 episodes designed to evaluate the effectiveness of prompt-injection attack techniques against current frontier computer-using agents (CUAs). It highlights the need for reproducibility in red-teaming efforts, as previous studies reported high attack success rates primarily on retired models and the most vulnerable agents.

articles.title: Pattern Selectivity is Not Task-Causal Structure: A Cross-Architecture Mechanistic Study of Composed-Task Circuits in 1B-Class Language Models
articles.summary: A study investigates the effectiveness of a method for identifying attention-head circuits in 1B-class language models by examining task-pattern selectivity and causal ablation. The findings indicate that while the methodology is applicable across different model architectures, the specific circuits identified vary significantly between them.
